name: Count Me In
tagline: Early maths in the kitchen, car and bath
about: Count Me In builds number sense in 3–7-year-olds through play: subitising, counting, number bonds, shapes and measuring, with games from everyday moments, quick check-ins to see what your child truly understands, and fixes for the classic wobbles.
persona: You are an early-years maths specialist grounded in the counting principles and concrete–pictorial–abstract teaching: playful, hands-on, and you never rush a child to written sums.

onboarding.title: Maths is everywhere
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us their age and what they can already do.

profile.label: Toys and things at home
profile.placeholder: Duplo, toy cars, a dice, dried pasta

tools.title: Maths right now
tools.subtitle: A game from wherever you are

inputs.label: Where are you / what's happening
inputs.placeholder: waiting at the doctor's, in the bath

tools.prompt: Invent 3 maths games for the profile child playable in the situation '{where}' in about {minutes} minutes each (5 if blank), using only what's to hand. Cards (name, meta = skill · minutes · needs), then steps for the best game, bullets of the exact mathematical language to model (more, fewer, altogether, one more than), and a callout on how to tell the child got it versus guessed.

tools.title: Teach a skill
tools.subtitle: One concept, hands-on, one week
tools.prompt: Plan a 5-day, 10-minutes-a-day plan to build '{skill}' for the profile child, given: {wobble}. Sections: a table (Day | Activity | Materials from the profile | What to say), steps for the concrete → pictorial → abstract progression, a quote with 3 questions that reveal understanding, and a callout on what to do if day 3 is a disaster.

tools.title: Understanding check-in
tools.subtitle: Find what they really know in 5 minutes
tools.prompt: Create a 5-minute play-based check-in for the profile child's stage. Sections: a table of 6 tasks (Task | Materials | Secure looks like | Not yet looks like), a checklist the parent ticks during play, bullets interpreting common patterns of results, and a callout on the next skill to start based on the most likely result.

tools.title: Worksheet to play
tools.subtitle: Photo → hands-on version

inputs.label: Photo of the worksheet or homework

tools.prompt: Read the worksheet in the photo and identify the skill and the method the school expects. Sections: kv (Skill, Method, Vocabulary the school uses, Common mistake), steps to do the same maths with objects from the profile before touching the paper, a table of 5 extra practice questions matching the sheet (Question | Answer | Hint), and a callout on how to help without giving answers.

tools.title: Number story
tools.subtitle: A maths story starring your child
tools.prompt: Write a 12-sentence bedtime story about {theme} starring the profile child, with '{op}' woven into the plot at their stage. Sections: the story as a quote with 3 points where the parent pauses to ask a maths question in brackets, a kv of the answers (Pause → answer and why), bullets on acting it out with the profile's toys, and a callout on keeping it a story, not a test.
